correction_brief:
MONTREAL.AI builds evidence-grounded scientific instruments. A new blinded-by-input, historical ExoClock study used archival ephemerides and timing inputs available by April 2023, 59 later calibration targets, and 106 distinct later confirmation targets. The released center with explicit reported marginal uncertainty and independently fitted calibration covered 96 of 106. Conventional weighted and robust refits each covered 93. A horizon-adaptive scaling of the weighted predictions covered 94 and missed the registered 90 percent gate. None earned an observing-time advantage. The 3-year old analysis cohort cannot qualify today's schedule. The separate domain USGS tool exactly integrated 28 published daily mean flow intervals and matched the government's published aggregate. Compact local 4B output no longer truncates, but none of its programs solved a fresh numerical case. The operator-assisted Codex construction exactly passed 42 held cases. Existing authorized resources are public archives, included Codex, CPU inference, and portable exact tools, with no telescope commitments, paid calls, or independently administered research host.

Correction from the verifier: 96 is a count out of 106 = 90.57%, not 96%. The operating gate is 90%. DSN communication logs are not measurements of this phenomenon. Identify one independent, dated primary evidence source appropriate to exoplanet transit timing or a different explicitly justified problem. Propose how the test could disconfirm a hypothesis. Previously revealed results are diagnostic only.
